title: When the product hides the evidence
question: Can an edit move its own evidence outside the read?
finding: In the CFTR example, a three-base insertion shifts the downstream anchor from [210, 222) to [213, 225). The observed read ends at 224. Under the same quality mask, changing the observation rule moved the treated-minus-mock lower endpoint from −10.09177 to +13.23196 percentage points.
scope: The comparison isolates the effect of the observation rule on the recorded contrast. The positive lower endpoint applies to the recorded set under the stated label assumptions.

title: Agreement can conceal different sequences
question: When callers agree, are they describing the same observed bases?
finding: Among 170,808 CFTR records resolved by three extraction rules, 83 yielded different coding strings. In 18 of those records, the native-local peptide labels still agreed. The sequence-level disagreement survives the label agreement.
scope: A label answers a target-specific question. Sequence correspondence also requires identifying the observed string and the rule that assigns it to the event.

title: Keep the unresolved records
question: What can be inferred when some events cannot be classified?
finding: Start with the original denominator N. If E records are accepted events and U remain unresolved, the lowest attainable proportion is E/N and the highest is (E+U)/N. The two-arm contrast uses the lower endpoint of one arm and the upper endpoint of the other.
scope: These are finite-record identification bounds under the stated accepted-label and completion assumptions. They describe what the observations allow, without a sampling confidence interpretation.

title: Certify a target across interpretations
question: How much disagreement can a certificate tolerate?
finding: Define the reference, score and admissible alignments before comparing their projections. A target is resolved when every admitted interpretation gives it the same value. A stricter common-string witness checks whether the extraction rules yield the same observed coding string.
scope: A certificate belongs to its declared target and domain. Two different strings can still support the same target value, while a broader reference or score domain can change the certificate.

title: Stability depends on what is compared
question: Can the contrast stay stable while individual calls change?
finding: The alignment sensitivity grid preserved positive lower contrast endpoints while changing some record-level labels. The two results coexist because the aggregate contrast and the membership of its resolved records answer different questions.
scope: Track the record identifiers alongside the contrast. Stability over the tested settings belongs to that finite grid and does not calibrate the probability that a molecular call is correct.

title: Test transfer in the right unit
question: What happens when we change the cohort or the acquisition?
finding: MP37 and MP38 tested transfer on reserved germline panels. A separate four-donor comparison showed the cost of filtering: an exact-length majority rule withdrew 25 of 26 discordant calls and 113 of 207 concordant calls. HiFi agreed with the benchmark at all 113 matched HG003/HG004 loci, including 15 Nanopore discordances.
scope: Keep donor, locus and acquisition visible. The benchmark tests germline genotype agreement in the declared panels. A favorable result has authority within that unit and design.

title: Distinguish a mate from molecular truth
question: What does an independent observation have to identify?
finding: The external paired-file audit linked 770,673 read pairs at the amplified-insert level. The proportion with both reads at 250 bases differed by 9.44 percentage points between libraries. In COL17A1 Clone3, retained spans support a six-base deletion with two equivalent placements. Each result identifies a different observation unit.
scope: Estimating editing accuracy on the original HEK3 or CFTR fragment requires independently informative evidence linked to that physical fragment. The audited historical records leave that quantity unestimated.

title: Reproduce the claim and test what would change it
question: How can a reviewer try to overturn the result?
finding: Follow a claim back to its input, event definition, counts and admissible interpretations. The public runner checks the archived counts and reconstructs the exact CFTR contrast. Retained-span reproduction and original FASTQ extraction are distinct operations with separate receipts.
scope: A recovered anchor inside the purportedly censored read or a corrected orientation that resolves a coding disagreement would revise the affected observation or contrast. The graph links those revision tests to the claims they concern.

title: From the claim to a reusable experiment
question: How can another researcher inspect and test this result?
finding: Open the 3D laboratory, follow the two-read CFTR leading case, and run the multi-input manifest. Preserve parameters, source identities and unresolved outcomes with each exported result.
scope: These tools expose and replay evidence. The three programme uses have different integration states; neither an interface nor a replay creates independent biological truth.

title: Start with a decision, not an interface
question: What should I do with my own counts?
finding: Define the event, preserve E/NE/U, compute the exact contrast and choose the next check. The guided report also exposes local discordance removal and concordance loss.
scope: Arithmetic and structural validation of declared inputs; the report does not independently authenticate labels.

title: Connect to function only through a verified link
question: Can the functional result calibrate these sequence calls?
finding: The published PE responses exceed the mock responses at condition level. However, six possible assignments of three functional labels change the sign and size of the apparent sequence-function correlation.
scope: Functional context is admitted; a paired correlation, same-pool identity and original-fragment truth remain unauthenticated.
